title: the failure drill under compose
note: Written by hand from the drill's records (failure-drill-2026-11-18/records/) and the orchestrator's log of the database nights. The drill reports and fixes nothing; each finding names the file that should change.

findings.claim: A database kill while a job runs leaves that job running for good: the worker's failure handler reads the job from the database, which is down, so the error escapes to the worker loop; nothing requeues the job until the orchestrator restarts and the requester is not told.
findings.place: services/orchestrator/core.py:566 (self.db.get in the except branch of _run), core.py:791-793 (_worker logs 'worker error' and goes on)
findings.expected: No lost job: an interrupted job is queued again or failed with a reason (T-689, D-456, D-532; plan 8 V12; D-1109)
findings.happened: In 2 of 3 database nights (the first full run and run 1 of the final) the mailed SCREEN GZQO stayed running past the 900 s window while the database and the orchestrator were healthy, and its 7 result mails were never sent; in full-disk run 1 the timer's INGEST stayed running the same way, so RETENTION never started. A restart of the orchestrator requeued each and it ended done (11 s, 46 s)

findings.claim: No runbook page says what to do when a job stays running after the database came back; the step that works (restart the orchestrator, whose start requeues the job) is written nowhere.
findings.place: docs/runbook/04-troubleshooting.md (a row for a job that stays running after a database restart)
findings.expected: A recovery that needs a person has a runbook row (card H-31; plan 8 V12)
findings.happened: The drill's person's step after the check (docker compose restart orchestrator) ended the stuck job; the troubleshooting table names restarts only for a job 'interrupted by a restart of the box N times'

findings.claim: When the adapter's ingest run ends while the database is down, its ingest.failed event cannot be audited (AuditUnavailable, in the adapter's log) and is not kept for later: the night's audit trail lacks the failure though the chain verifies.
findings.place: services/adapter/run_job.py (the failure's audit append) with libs/tb_common/audit_writer.py (the journal lives in the same database)
findings.expected: Every state change of a night is audited (SPEC 10.2; D-394); the register's rule: an audit trail that can be wrong is High
findings.happened: Full-disk run 1 of the final drill: the adapter logged 'ingest.failed could not be audited' with error AuditUnavailable while PostgreSQL was restarting
